newsitem.title: USA: Washington state votes on $425 mln stadium plan.
newsitem.headline: Washington state votes on $425 mln stadium plan.

text.p: Washington state voters went to the polls Tuesday to decide the fate of a proposed $425 million Seattle football stadium in an election contest that pits poorly funded opponents against billionaire Paul Allen.
The polls, which opened at 0700 local were scheduled to close at 2000. Voters in most of the state's counties have, however, already cast their ballots by mail.

A carefully constructed tax package and massive television advertising campaign appear to have given the stadium proposal at least an even chance of passing in the special election, according to recent opinion polls.
Allen, worth more than $13 billion as co-founder of Microsoft Corp, already counts the Portland Trail Blazers basketball team among his many holdings.

In April 1996 he bought an option on the Seattle Seahawks to keep the team from being moved out of town. But he has insisted he will walk away from the deal without a new stadium to replace the 21-year-old Kingdome.
Allen has contributed nearly $5 million to the pro-stadium campaign, allowing one of the most expensive television advertising blitzes in state history.
Stadium opponents have been able to raise only about $200,000 for a few cable television ads.

The stadium package, approved narrowly by the state legislature, includes $101 million from existing sales taxes, $127 million from lottery games, $56 million in stadium admissions and parking taxes and $40 million in hotel room taxes.
Allen has agreed to contribute $50 million of his own money and $50 million from the sale of seat licenses as well as cover any cost overruns.
